chunks: And from him, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Indeed, upon one of you, when the night has passed halfway, is to rise and pray his prayer as a single unit, thirteen rak'ahs. Then if he wishes, he sits and supplicates; and if he wishes, he sleeps; and if he wishes, he goes wherever he wishes."
And it is recommended that the person does not sleep after these two rak'ahs and occupies himself with supplication and glorification, for indeed sleep at this time is disliked.
ai.seo_question: What is the number of rak'ahs in the night prayer and what should one do after completing it?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam al-Baqir (AS), this hadith establishes the canonical structure of the thirteen-rak'ah night prayer, emphasizing the spiritual significance of the time after midnight (Wusta al-Layl). While it permits flexibility in post-prayer conduct, Shia jurisprudence highlights the preference for remaining in a state of devotion through supplication and dhikr rather than sleeping, reflecting the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt's nocturnal worship.
